20vc.name: 20VC
20vc.description: Long interviews with investors and founders about how funds actually decide, how boards work, and what a raise looks like from both sides of the table.

a16z.name: Andreessen Horowitz
a16z.description: Talks from the a16z orbit on markets, AI, consumer products, and the mechanics of building a company that can take a category.

aaronross.name: Aaron Ross
aaronross.description: Outbound sales system behind Predictable Revenue: specialized roles, cold outreach, and how a small team books meetings without a founder doing every call.

acquired.name: Acquired
acquired.description: Company histories told as business case studies: how a firm found its wedge, survived a near-death, and compounded into a franchise.

andrew-chen.name: Andrew Chen
andrew-chen.description: Network effects and the cold-start problem, from the Uber growth years to marketplace expansion. Useful when you are asking how a product gets its first users and then does not stall.

april-dunford.name: April Dunford
april-dunford.description: Positioning talks: how to pick a market, name the alternatives, and stop sounding like every other B2B product in the category.

april-dunford-blog.name: April Dunford (writing)
april-dunford-blog.description: Blog essays on positioning, sales narratives, and the difference between a feature list and a story a buyer can repeat.

belfort.name: Jordan Belfort
belfort.description: Straight-line persuasion, tonality, and the unglamorous parts of closing. Treat as a sales-craft corpus, not a morality guide.

brad-feld.name: Brad Feld
brad-feld.description: Startup boards, venture partnering, and the Boulder thesis. Feld talks like an operator who has sat on both sides of the cap table.

brian-balfour.name: Brian Balfour
brian-balfour.description: Growth loops versus funnels, product-channel fit, and the path to a $100M product. Reforge-era thinking in talk form.

chris-voss.name: Chris Voss
chris-voss.description: Negotiation from the FBI playbook: calibrated questions, tactical empathy, no-oriented questions. Maps cleanly onto sales and partnership talks.

codyschneider.name: Cody Schneider
codyschneider.description: Small e-commerce and side-business ideas with concrete unit economics. Useful as a foil to venture-scale advice.

custdev.name: Customer development (mixed)
custdev.description: A small mixed set of customer-development talks that did not land in a named series.

custdev-jtbd-moesta.name: Jobs to Be Done (Bob Moesta)
custdev-jtbd-moesta.description: Switch interviews, pushing and pulling forces, and the timeline of a buying decision. The practical JTBD corpus.

custdev-lennys.name: Lenny's Podcast (custdev slice)
custdev-lennys.description: Lenny Rachitsky interviews that were pulled specifically for customer-development and product-market-fit craft.

custdev-mfm.name: My First Million (custdev slice)
custdev-mfm.description: Sam Parr and Shaan Puri riffing on businesses, distribution, and the weird ideas that actually print. Pulled for customer and market instinct, not for the bits.

custdev-momtest.name: The Mom Test
custdev-momtest.description: Rob Fitzpatrick's method for talking to users without fooling yourself: ask about their life, not your idea.

custdev-yc.name: Y Combinator (custdev slice)
custdev-yc.description: YC talks and office hours that were tagged for customer development: talking to users, finding a wedge, not scaling a ghost.

dalio.name: Ray Dalio
dalio.description: Principles, machine-like decision making, and how Bridgewater thinks about credit, cycles, and disagreement.

dankoe.name: Dan Koe
dankoe.description: One-person internet businesses, writing as distribution, and building a personal media company without a headcount.

danmartell.name: Dan Martell
danmartell.description: SaaS operations, buying back time, and the coaching lens on a founder who is the bottleneck.

david-sacks.name: David Sacks
david-sacks.description: Enterprise sales, PayPal mafia operating style, and later-stage company building. Mix of craft and punditry; the sales pieces are the ones to mine.

elena-verna.name: Elena Verna
elena-verna.description: Growth operator talks: loops, self-serve, and what breaks when you bolt a growth team onto a sales-led company.

firstround.name: First Round Capital
firstround.description: Review and Review-adjacent talks: early-stage operating advice from founders and the First Round network, denser than most VC content.

flywheel-founders.name: Flywheels and network effects
flywheel-founders.description: A curated set around Jim Collins' flywheel, blitzscaling, Hooked, and marketplace cold starts. One of the better strategy packs in the corpus.

garyvee.name: Gary Vaynerchuk
garyvee.description: Attention, day-trading social platforms, and the unromantic work of posting. Loud, repetitive, and still a primary source on distribution as a skill.

girard.name: Joe Girard
girard.description: Old-school personal selling: follow-up, volume, and treating every customer as a future referral. A contrast to modern PLG talk.

hormozi.name: Alex Hormozi
hormozi.description: Offers, pricing, and gym-to-software generalizations. Best mined for how he packages a promise, not for industry specifics.

kunal-shah.name: Kunal Shah
kunal-shah.description: CRED and the Indian consumer: trust, status, and why some products only work in a specific social stack.

lencioni.name: Patrick Lencioni
lencioni.description: Teams, meetings, and the five dysfunctions. Organizational craft rather than market craft.

lennys-podcast.name: Lenny's Podcast
lennys-podcast.description: Product, growth, and craft interviews. One of the densest modern sources on how good product orgs actually work.

lochhead.name: Christopher Lochhead
lochhead.description: Category design: do not join a market, make one. Play Bigger in talk form.

markroberge.name: Mark Roberge
markroberge.description: HubSpot's sales machine: hiring scorecards, onboarding ramps, and the handoff between inbound and outbound.

marktilbury.name: Mark Tilbury
marktilbury.description: Youth-facing money and small-business content. Lower signal than the operator talks, kept because it shows how business advice gets packaged for beginners.

meddicc.name: MEDDICC
meddicc.description: Enterprise qualification: metrics, economic buyer, decision process, paper process, implicate the pain, champion. The standard B2B close framework.

nfx.name: NFX
nfx.description: The network-effects manual: types of nfx, defensibility, and why most 'community' products do not have one.

paul-graham.name: Paul Graham
paul-graham.description: Essays and talks on startups, wealth, and what YC selects for. The closest thing this corpus has to a canon.

productled.name: ProductLed
productled.description: Product-led growth teardowns, time-to-value, and what a self-serve motion looks like when it is not a slide.

profitwell.name: ProfitWell / Paddle
profitwell.description: Retention, pricing research, and SaaS metrics from Patrick Campbell's orbit.

saastr.name: SaaStr
saastr.description: Jason Lemkin and guests on the operating reality of B2B SaaS: sales hiring, burn, expansion, and the years after product-market fit.

sales-cognism.name: Cognism
sales-cognism.description: Modern B2B outbound: data, sequences, and how a sales-intel company teaches prospecting.

sales-miner.name: Sales Miner
sales-miner.description: High-volume sales training clips. Noisy, repetitive, and still a usable sample of how outbound is taught at scale.

sales-patrickdang.name: Patrick Dang
sales-patrickdang.description: B2B closing and discovery, closer to SMB/mid-market than MEDDICC enterprise.

sales-scripter.name: Sales Scripter
sales-scripter.description: Cold-call scripts, objection handling, and appointment setting. One of the largest slices in the corpus; treat it as a script library, not as strategy.

sales-superhuman.name: Superhuman selling
sales-superhuman.description: High-tempo sales training. Pair with the MEDDICC and Cognism sets if you are comparing methodologies.

sam-blond.name: Sam Blond
sam-blond.description: Operator-level sales leadership: hiring AEs, forecasting, and running a team that does not live in the CRM.

stephfrance.name: Steph France
stephfrance.description: Founder-facing growth: Meta ads tests, hidden SaaS niches, and later AI-agent use cases. Practical more than theoretical.

stratechery.name: Stratechery (Ben Thompson)
stratechery.description: Aggregation theory and the structural pieces behind consumer internet businesses. Short set, high density.

wolfofwallst.name: Wolf of Wall Street (Belfort talks)
wolfofwallst.description: Another Belfort-branded slice of sales and persuasion talks, kept separate because it was collected as its own session.

ycombinator.name: Y Combinator
ycombinator.description: How to Start a Startup and later YC talks: the official early-stage playbook, from talking to users to not dying.

yamalkevich.name: Egor Yamalkevich
yamalkevich.description: Russian-language founder talks from the VMSTE orbit: building in public, community, and the CIS path from employee to founder.

indie-hackers.name: Indie Hackers Podcast
indie-hackers.description: Interviews with bootstrapped and mostly-bootstrapped founders who share revenue, distribution, and the unglamorous middle years. One of the best sources in this repo for pattern-hunting across many small businesses.

practical-product.name: Practical Product
practical-product.description: Product-management craft: first PM problems, specs people will read, hiring, and remote product leadership.

starter-story.name: Starter Story
starter-story.description: Founder write-ups of real businesses: how the idea appeared, what it cost, what it earns, which channel worked. The structured metadata is often empty; the body text is where the numbers live. Original interviews remain copyright Starter Story; they are here for research and pattern analysis, with a link back to each page.

yc-companies.name: Y Combinator companies
yc-companies.description: Public YC directory snapshot: name, batch, location, team size, tags, status. The cleanest structured company table in the set.
yc-companies.license_note: Public directory. Facts about companies; YC owns the presentation.

sec-edgar.name: SEC EDGAR (Form D and related)
sec-edgar.description: US private placement filings. Amounts, dates, and exemption types for companies raising under Regulation D.

fund-holdings.name: Fund holdings inferred from Form D
fund-holdings.description: Attempt to roll Form D filings up to funds and their recent deals. Many rows still have unresolved names; treat as a raw join table, not a finished Crunchbase.
fund-holdings.license_note: Derived from US government public records.

companies-house.name: UK Companies House
companies-house.description: UK registered companies relevant to the collection: names, locations, and status from the public register.

openbook-vc.name: OpenVC / public fund profiles
openbook-vc.description: Publicly listed funds with thesis, cheque size, and geography. Small but usable as a fund rolodex.
openbook-vc.license_note: Public profiles; original site owns the presentation.

product-hunt.name: Product Hunt launches
product-hunt.description: A thin slice of product launches. Not a full PH dump; enough to join a launch date to a company.

techcrunch-rss.name: TechCrunch funding RSS
techcrunch-rss.description: Funding headlines from the TechCrunch feed, kept as a news tick, not as a complete round database.
techcrunch-rss.license_note: Headlines and links; full articles stay on TechCrunch.

cis-curated.name: Hand-curated CIS / Israel / GCC lists
cis-curated.description: Small lists of notable Russian, Ukrainian, Israeli, and GCC tech companies plus CIS funds and accelerators. Hand-built, not scraped at scale.

corp-cis.name: CIS corporates
corp-cis.description: Larger CIS tech and internet companies, used as incumbents against which startups in the region are compared.

corp-eu.name: European corporates
corp-eu.description: A short list of European incumbents for regional context.

corp-giant.name: Global giants
corp-giant.description: A handful of global tech incumbents, kept as reference points, not as a market map.

corp-israel.name: Israeli tech companies
corp-israel.description: Notable Israeli firms for the high-trust / deep-tech side of the regional set.

corp-mena.name: MENA corporates
corp-mena.description: A short MENA incumbent list for regional comparison.

corp-midsize.name: Mid-size corporates
corp-midsize.description: Mid-size firms that sit between startup and giant. Useful when a founder story needs a realistic acquirer or competitor.

geo-enrichment.name: Geographic enrichment
geo-enrichment.description: Lat/lon and region tags joined onto companies in the set. Use it to plot, not as a gazetteer.

events.name: Company events
events.description: A timeline of public signals (YC batch, recognition, and similar) keyed to company ids. Join to yc-companies and sec-edgar.
events.origin: derived from the company sources above

book-catalog.name: Book catalog
book-catalog.description: Reading list of startup and business books that sat in the local cache. Catalog and short quotes only; full files are not in the repo. Links go to Wikipedia, Open Library, or the author's page.
